sections.eyebrow: Initial Financial Decision Assessment | Big Financial Decision
sections.heading: Before a major financial decision, see the options and risks more clearly
paragraphs: Buying or selling a significant asset, making a new investment, arranging finance or expanding a business can affect your liquidity, commitments and future plans.

DNH’s initial assessment is designed to understand the decision, your broader circumstances and whether the request fits our services. Where there is a suitable fit and mutual agreement, the route for a specialist review of the options and implications can then be defined.
sections.note: The starting point is a better understanding of the issue—not a definitive answer or a guaranteed outcome.

media.alt: Analytical setting for reviewing a major financial decision

sections.heading: What financial decision are you approaching?
paragraphs: Some financial decisions are more than a straightforward choice; they can reshape capital, commitments or future plans.
If one of the following situations feels familiar, an initial assessment may be an appropriate place to begin.

items.title: Investing and changing assets
items.description: You are considering buying, selling or reallocating capital and want to understand how the decision may affect your overall wealth structure.

items.title: Financing and new commitments
items.description: You are considering borrowing, increasing debt or using financial resources and need to assess the future costs and commitments.

items.title: Business expansion or restructuring
items.description: You are planning to expand, introduce capital or change the financial structure of a business and need to understand the implications.

items.title: Family wealth decisions
items.description: You are making a decision about family assets, capital preservation or future financial needs that may affect several people and their plans.

sections.closing: What matters is not only the size of the amount, but how the decision may affect your financial position and future choices.

sections.eyebrow: Five dimensions of a financial decision
sections.heading: Before you decide, these five questions need to be clear
paragraphs: A financial decision should not be judged only by price, expected return or the appeal of an opportunity.
A more complete review considers five dimensions together.

items.title: The issue
items.question: What, precisely, are you deciding?
items.description: Is this an investment, a liquidity requirement, a change in asset structure or a choice between several routes?

items.title: Risk
items.question: What could develop differently from what you expect?
items.description: Identify the conditions that could affect capital, commitments or the outcome of the decision.

items.title: Liquidity
items.question: After the decision, what liquid resources will remain available, and what time, cost or constraints would be involved in converting other assets to cash?

items.title: Time horizon
items.question: When will you need access to your financial resources?
items.description: Consider the investment period, the possible return of capital, and both short- and long-term needs.

items.title: Scenarios
items.question: If circumstances change, what consequences could follow?
items.description: Examine plausible situations and the decision’s sensitivity to changing assumptions.

sections.closing: These five dimensions bring the important aspects of a choice into view without assuming that the outcome is certain in advance.

sections.heading: The initial assessment begins the review; it does not complete it
paragraphs: Not every financial decision requires an extensive analytical engagement from the outset.
DNH first establishes the subject and your broader circumstances so that the appropriate type of specialist review—and a possible next step—can be identified.

sections.heading: The best choice is not always the option with the highest return
paragraphs: Two options may both appear attractive in terms of potential return while creating very different levels of liquidity, cost, risk and financial flexibility.
Considering those differences helps prevent a decision from being judged by a single measure.

items.title: Costs and commitments
items.description: What new costs or financial responsibilities would each option create?

items.title: Liquidity
items.description: After the decision, what liquid resources remain available, and what time, cost or constraints would be involved in converting other assets to cash?

items.title: Risk and adverse implications
items.description: If circumstances change unfavourably, which part of the capital would be affected?

items.title: Future flexibility
items.description: Would this choice restrict your ability to pursue opportunities or change course later?

sections.closing: An appropriate choice must be considered in light of the real objectives, financial circumstances and constraints of the individual or business.

sections.heading: What happens if conditions do not develop as expected?
paragraphs: Before committing capital, reviewing several plausible situations can make the constraints easier to understand.
Scenario analysis is not an attempt to predict the future with certainty. Its purpose is to clarify assumptions and the possible implications of a decision.

items.title: Expected conditions
items.description: If income, costs and markets develop in line with the initial assumptions, what implications would the decision have?

items.title: Delayed access to funds
items.description: If an asset sale, income receipt or return of capital takes longer than expected, how would liquidity and commitments be affected?

items.title: Changing economic conditions
items.description: If financing costs, inflation or market conditions change, which parts of the decision would need to be reconsidered?

sections.closing: These scenarios are considered to improve understanding of risk and constraints—not to create anxiety or prescribe a particular decision.

sections.eyebrow: Who the initial assessment is for
sections.heading: Who may benefit from an initial financial decision assessment?
paragraphs: This route is intended for people facing a decision that could materially affect their capital, wealth structure or the future of a business, and who want to understand the issue more precisely before acting.

items.title: Individuals and families
items.description: You need to consider the options and possible implications of buying or selling an asset, managing wealth or making a family financial decision.

items.title: Investors and wealth owners
items.description: You are approaching an investment or a change in capital allocation and want to examine risk, liquidity and alignment with your objectives.

items.title: Executives and business owners
items.description: You are making a decision about financing, capital allocation or expansion and need to understand the financial implications.

sections.heading: How does an initial financial decision assessment begin?
paragraphs: You do not need to prepare every financial document before getting started.
A short explanation of the issue and the broader circumstances is enough for an initial review and to establish an appropriate route.

steps.title: Introduce the issue
steps.subtitle: Describe the decision you are facing
steps.description: Explain the decision ahead, the objective you are pursuing, and your most important uncertainty or concern.

steps.title: Initial review
steps.subtitle: Understand the context and fit
steps.description: The subject, urgency and broad information provided are reviewed to identify the matters that require closer attention.

steps.title: Define the next route
steps.subtitle: Determine the appropriate type of review

sections.result: A clearer understanding of the decision, its main uncertainties and the possible route for further engagement—not a full analytical report or definitive investment advice.

sections.heading: Which service may be relevant after the assessment?
paragraphs: Financial decisions do not all require the same kind of advice. Depending on the issue and your circumstances, one of DNH’s specialist areas may be relevant for further review.

items.title: Private Wealth Strategy
items.description: Review the alignment of wealth structure, assets and financial objectives.

items.title: Portfolio Intelligence
items.description: Understand existing asset composition, risk concentration and liquidity.

items.title: Strategic Financial Advisory
items.description: Review significant decisions involving financing, liquidity and business capital structure.

items.title: Risk Management & Wealth Protection
items.description: Identify vulnerabilities and prioritise financial risks.

items.title: Macro & Market Advisory
items.description: Assess how economic developments may affect a financial or business issue.

items.title: Executive Briefings
items.description: Conduct a focused review of an important financial or strategic decision at executive level.

sections.eyebrow: Expertise and trust in financial decision-making
sections.heading: Important decisions require specialist judgement and responsible review
paragraphs: DNH is built on the experience and analytical perspective of Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani, Wealth Architect and Strategic Financial Adviser.
She holds a PhD in Financial Engineering and a Master’s degree in Financial Management, with more than 15 years of financial management experience and over 7 years in investment and asset management.
